title: TS SDK streaming middleware: progress events & deterministic handoff between AsyncIterator and ReadableStream
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: SDK consumers need ergonomic interop between WHATWG ReadableStream (browser/deno/node:stream/web) and AsyncIterator-based consumption patterns across runtime boundaries. Current adapters are ad-hoc, lose progress signals, and have ambiguous cancellation/handshake semantics which cause truncated uploads, leaked controllers, or double-closing of upstream sockets.

Goal: Define and implement a small middleware surface in the TypeScript SDK that: (1) exposes progress events and optional structured metadata from streaming responses, (2) provides deterministic handoff semantics when converting between AsyncIterator and ReadableStream (both directions), (3) preserves backpressure and cancellation propagation, (4) is small surface-area and backwards compatible with existing SDK patterns, and (5) works consistently across Node, Deno, and browsers (polyfilled where necessary).

Proposed API sketches (developer-facing):
- fromReadableStream<T>(stream: ReadableStream<T>, opts?: {signal?: AbortSignal, onProgress?: (meta: string|number|Record<string,any>) => void}) : AsyncIterable<T | ProgressEvent>
- toReadableStream<T>(source: AsyncIterable<T | ProgressEvent>, opts?: {highWaterMark?: number, signal?: AbortSignal}) : ReadableStream<T>
- createStreamMiddleware(options?: {emitProgressAsEvents?: boolean, progressFrameKey?: string}) : Middleware  // pluggable for SDK pipeline

Semantics highlights:
- ProgressEvent shape is opt-in and namespaced so callers can filter yields. Default shape: {type: 'progress', total?: number, delta?: number, bytes?: number, detail?: string}. It will be yielded interleaved with data when using AsyncIterable mode, and dispatched via onProgress for ReadableStream->AsyncIterator conversions when emitProgressAsEvents=false.
- Cancellation: upstream AbortSignal must be wired through. If consumer aborts, we send a deterministic closure handshake: send 'CLOSE' frame on the framing layer (if used), then abort upstream after pending flush window (configurable short timeout). This prevents premature socket tear-down observed in some server stacks.
- Backpressure: when converting AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream, the adapter uses controller.desiredSize to pace iteration and awaits when desiredSize <= 0. When converting ReadableStream -> AsyncIterator, the adapter pauses pull/read if consumer falls behind (via internal queue threshold).
- Error propagation: any error thrown from either side is rethrown to the other side and results in immediate abort of the paired controller; error includes standardized code (RINF_STREAM_ERR) and contextual metadata.

Compatibility notes:
- Node: prefer native stream/web ReadableStream where available (Node 18+). For older Node environments, include a small internal polyfill that implements whatwg semantics required by the adapter.
- Browser: rely on built-in ReadableStream; ensure no reliance on Node-only APIs (Buffer, process.nextTick).
- Deno: use ReadableStream API.

Deliverables: implementation in packages/sdk-js/stream-adapters, unit tests, e2e demo sample (examples/stream-handoff), documentation page with code snippets and migration notes, micro-bench to measure latency and memory across adapters.
acceptance_criteria: adapter implements fromReadableStream and toReadableStream with documented options
progress events exposed via both yield shape and onProgress callback (configurable)
abort signals from consumer propagate to upstream and vice versa with deterministic handshake
unit tests cover cancellation, error propagation, and backpressure for Node/browser/Deno runtimes
example repo demonstrates a browser -> server -> SDK flow where progress events are surfaced to UI
docs page with migration guide from older ad-hoc adapters and code samples added to SDK docs
benchmark showing no >10% median token-latency regression vs current adapter in typical small-chunk workloads
decisions: emitProgressAsEvents default: true (but can yield progress objects when caller opts in)
use AbortController-based cancellation plumbing; avoid custom event emitters for cancellation
framing of progress metadata: lightweight JSON frames prefixed by 0x1F (unit separator) in binary paths; plain object in stream-mode
do not expose low-level controller APIs on public surface to keep compatibility stable
implementation_notes: internal API should live under packages/sdk-js/stream-adapters and be exported from '@redwood/sdk/streams'
prefer async generator implementation for fromReadableStream to allow for easy try/catch/finally and early returns
use a bounded internal queue for ReadableStream->AsyncIterator conversion with configurable maxEntries (default 32) to avoid unbounded memory growth
when yielding ProgressEvent objects, we prefix them with a small discriminator field {__rinf_type: 'progress'} to avoid colliding with user payloads
add small integration shim for older Node by using 'stream/web' polyfill only when global ReadableStream is absent
add feature-flag guarded rollout and an opt-in "experimentalStreamingMiddleware" config in SDK client constructor for first-stage testing
test_plan: unit: happy path conversions (ReadbleStream->AsyncIterator and back) with string and binary chunks
unit: progress events interleaving and filtering; consumers can ignore progress yields without breaking iteration
stress: start 100 concurrent adapters with simulated slow consumers to verify memory threshold and backpressure behavior
e2e: example browser upload with progress UI wired to onProgress and AsyncIterator consumer reading data on the server side
ci: add matrix for Node 16/18/20 browsers (chrome stable ec) and Deno latest; run perf micro-bench and assert latency regression <10%
